reference.source: ESC/ERS Guidelines for Pulmonary Hypertension / Nunn's Applied Respiratory Physiology
clinicalPearls: A rare pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension grouped with pulmonary veno-occlusive disease because of overlapping histology, clinical behaviour, and shared biallelic EIF2AK4 mutations
Characterised by capillary proliferation within the alveolar walls that infiltrates and obstructs the pulmonary microvasculature
Presents with progressive exertional breathlessness and features of pulmonary hypertension, often more severe than the modest catheterisation pressures suggest
High-resolution CT typically shows diffuse centrilobular ground-glass nodules, septal thickening, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy
The pulmonary artery wedge pressure is characteristically normal despite radiological signs suggestive of post-capillary congestion, reflecting disease distal to the true measuring point
Targeted pulmonary vasodilators must be used with great caution or avoided, as they can precipitate severe and sometimes fatal pulmonary oedema
Definitive treatment is lung transplantation, and early referral is essential given the poor prognosis
reference.pathophysiology: Pulmonary capillary haemangiomatosis is characterised by uncontrolled proliferation of thin-walled capillaries that infiltrate the alveolar septa, bronchovascular bundles, pleura, and the walls of pulmonary veins and arteries. This proliferating capillary network encroaches on and obstructs the microvascular bed, raising pulmonary vascular resistance and producing pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension. Because the proliferating vessels compress and involve the post-capillary venules, the disorder shares physiology and imaging features with pulmonary veno-occlusive disease, and many familial cases carry biallelic loss-of-function mutations in EIF2AK4. The key clinical hazard is that the obstruction lies downstream of the arterioles, so pulmonary vasodilators increase flow into a fixed distal obstruction and can flood the capillary bed, precipitating acute pulmonary oedema.
additionalDifferentials: Idiopathic or heritable pulmonary arterial hypertension
Pulmonary hypertension due to left heart disease (group 2)
Diffuse parenchymal lung disease with pulmonary hypertension
additionalInvestigations: High-resolution CT of the chest for centrilobular ground-glass nodules, septal lines, and lymphadenopathy
Right heart catheterisation showing pre-capillary haemodynamics with a normal wedge pressure
Genetic testing for biallelic EIF2AK4 mutations
Pulmonary function tests, characteristically with a markedly reduced diffusing capacity
Arterial blood gases and exercise oxygen assessment
Ventilation-perfusion scan to exclude chronic thromboembolic disease
redFlags: Development of pulmonary oedema after starting targeted pulmonary vasodilator therapy
Signs of decompensated right heart failure
reference.prognosis: The prognosis is poor, with progressive pulmonary hypertension and limited response to medical therapy, and death from right heart failure or vasodilator-precipitated pulmonary oedema. Lung transplantation is the only definitive treatment and offers the best chance of survival, so early referral is critical.
pitfalls: Prescribing pulmonary vasodilators without recognising the risk of precipitating fatal pulmonary oedema
Misdiagnosing the disease as idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension and treating it accordingly
Overlooking the diagnostic clues of a very low diffusing capacity and characteristic CT changes
Delaying transplant referral because catheterisation pressures appear only modestly raised
Failing to consider a shared spectrum with pulmonary veno-occlusive disease and the EIF2AK4 genotype
references: ESC/ERS Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension
management: Refer early for lung transplantation, which is the only definitive treatment given the poor progressive course
Use targeted pulmonary vasodilators with great caution or avoid them, as increasing flow into the fixed distal obstruction can precipitate severe pulmonary oedema
Supportive treatment with diuretics for right heart failure and oxygen for hypoxaemia
Undertake any vasodilator trial only in an expert centre with close monitoring for pulmonary oedema
Genetic testing and counselling for biallelic EIF2AK4 mutations, with family screening
Right heart catheterisation and serial assessment to define pre-capillary haemodynamics and track progression
Coordinate care in a specialist pulmonary hypertension and transplant centre
